thread:
Maya: FYI an enterprise customer in EMEA reported repeated SSE disconnects when a user unlocks their phone while switching from station WiFi -> carrier. Happens reliably ~20-30s after unlock. They see partial output and then stream stops with no final event.
Sam: Do we have a request id + logs?
Maya: request_id=rx-7f9b3c, app logs show `EventSource.onerror` then `connection closed` and client reports code=1006. Server logs around the time show: 
```
[2026-03-12T09:41:15Z] rx-7f9b3c stream started model=gptx-v1 route=/v1/stream
[2026-03-12T09:41:55Z] rx-7f9b3c keepalive_sent
[2026-03-12T09:41:58Z] rx-7f9b3c client_disconnected (grace_period expired)
```
Sam: Interesting that server logs 'grace_period expired' — could be idle timeout. Do they use token refresh that triggers an auth refresh mid-stream?
Maya: App team confirmed tokens rotate every 60s after unlock (they refresh aggressively). They also do a background reconnect attempt.
Priya: @Maya can you repro with a simple curl SSE client and reproduce a teardown on token rotation? If yes, try reproducing with a constant Authorization header vs refreshed header.
Maya: Repro steps I used:
1) run this on Android device connected to station WiFi
2) lock phone, wait 5s, unlock which triggers token refresh in app
3) observe SSE stop after ~25s
Curl repro I used: 
```
# baseline (no refresh):
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gptx-v1&prompt=hello"
# simulated refresh: after 20s start a second curl with new token then kill first client
```
Result: first client sees partial chunks and then stops without final event.
Diego: Could the client-side behavior be aggressively tearing TCP when it re-issues auth? Some mobile stacks close the socket when they re-init auth headers. Also some carrier NATs create new 5-tuple and middlebox kills old flows.
Sam: Do we see mismatched session ids or repeated `open_stream` for the same client id in logs?
Maya: For rx-7f9b3c I see a new connection logged as rx-7f9b3c-2 about 10s after unlock. Server then picks the newest connection and marks the old one as replaced -> `consumer_replaced` then `consumer_closed`. But client complains about partial response and billing counts that partial tokens.
Priya: Billing semantics aside, from reliability POV we should support in-protocol reconnection without losing final event. Two quick mitigations: extend auth TTL for mobile unlocked flows (~5m), or add a short grace window on server to continue streaming to old connection for N seconds while new connection hydrates (if we can tie them to same session id).
Sam: Could we also add a keepalive ping frequency change? If client is getting partials then socket non-EOF, we could send a ping immediately after reconnect to flush final chunks.
Diego: Ops note: proxy & WAF between carrier and our infra sometimes rewrites SSE chunk boundaries. Need to check if any 502/timeout from upstream coincides. @support-bot can you fetch edge proxy logs for rx-7f9b3c timeframe?
support-bot: Fetching logs for request_id=rx-7f9b3c window=2026-03-12T09:40:00Z..2026-03-12T09:45:00Z ... 
support-bot: Found transient 504 from gateway at 2026-03-12T09:41:59Z for client_ip=10.78.45.21 (carrier NAT).
Maya: That 504 lines up exactly with the disconnect in the app. Carrier NAT + token refresh + new SYN from mobile when switching radios might be a trifecta.
Sam: Action items:
- Maya: capture a pcap on device or request an engineer on-site to reproduce with tcpdump (priority).
- Priya: add short-term change to auth TTL for unlocked mobile flows and monitor error rate (config flag).
- Diego: investigate whether gateway config can be tuned to avoid aggressive 504s on mid-flow 5-tuple changes.
- Platform: consider server-side `session_id` bind so new auth can claim stream without aborting final event; design doc next week.
Maya: For customer communication: they want a workaround now — recommend they disable immediate token rotation on unlock and enable exponential backoff on reconnect attempts.
Sam: Good. Also log a follow-up ticket to evaluate billing treatment of aborted partial streams.
Priya: I'll draft a small runbook for mobile app teams about SSE reconnect best practices (keepalive, avoid immediate token swap, sticky session id).
Maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Diego: :eyes: ping me once you have pcap, I can correlate with gateway traces.
Maya: uploaded pcap and app logs to the escalations ticket: https://redwood.internal/ticket/INC-4821
Sam: I'll loop SOC if we see more customers with same pattern.
